title: The Painting That Told the Truth

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An artist paints a hard chapter of village history on the meeting hut: keep the painting, or ask for something celebratory.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has painted the long wall of the meeting hut with the story of the year of the great hunger, long ago: the empty gardens, the families who left, the ones who stayed. It is beautiful and very sad. (friend) says the meeting hut should have happy pictures. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The painting stays. People stop in front of it, quiet. Children ask what happened, and are told. Some elders cry in front of it. Some are glad it is finally said. (friend) comes to like it, slowly.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) paints over part of it with the year of the great harvest that followed. The hunger is still there, at one end, smaller. The two stories sit side by side. (subject) thinks that is a lie of balance. (friend) thinks it is hope.
